name: manual_1ba604
claim: Two real, reusable mypy technical gotchas found while adding strict type-checking to orama-system's bin/orama-system/cidf/ (relevant to any repo with a similarly hyphenated directory or dual/inconsistent import styles): (1) a directory name containing a hyphen (orama-system) is not a valid Python package identifier, so mypy fails immediately with "contains __init__.py but is not a valid Python package name" unless run with --namespace-packages and --explicit-package-bases (or the pyproject.toml [tool.mypy] equivalents namespace_packages=true, explicit_package_bases=true) -- this is not a bug in the code, it's a structural fact about the directory name that must be worked around in tooling config. (2) When the same importable module is reachable from two different MYPYPATH roots under two different dotted names (e.g. a file importable as both core.content_insertion_framework via one root and cidf.core.content_insertion_framework via another, because two files in the same codebase genuinely use inconsistent import styles for the same package), mypy fails with "Source file found twice under different module names" if both roots are given in a single invocation. Fix: run mypy separately per file-group, using only the MYPYPATH root that group's own imports actually rely on, and add --follow-imports=silent to a later invocation that transitively reaches files an earlier invocation already fully checked -- this avoids re-triggering the same ambiguity while still getting full checking on each group's own signatures. Do not try to force one unified invocation to handle both import styles at once; that's fighting the codebase's own real inconsistency rather than working around it cleanly.

decisions.notes: Specific, reusable mypy technical knowledge that saves rediscovering two real gotchas from scratch in this or a similarly-structured repo.
